alt: Panorama of the Colca Canyon with steep terraced walls and the river far below
caption: The Colca Canyon, one of the deepest in the Americas, seen from the rim near Cabanaconde. Two days on foot into and out of it, sleeping at the oasis on the canyon floor, are the physical core of this trip.

alt: An Andean condor in flight over the Colca Canyon
caption: An Andean condor riding the morning thermals at Cruz del Cóndor. Birds usually appear between about 08:00 and 10:00, so the trek is timed to be at the viewpoint at first light.

alt: Green oasis with palms and simple lodges on the floor of the Colca Canyon
caption: The green oasis on the canyon floor where the trek sleeps, about 1,000 m below Cabanaconde. Lodging here is basic bungalows and tent pitches, and the climb out the next morning takes roughly three hours.

commonsFile: File:ARE - Blue corridor in Santa Catalina Monastery, Arequipa, Peru, 2013.jpg
alt: Blue-painted corridor inside the Santa Catalina Monastery in Arequipa
caption: A blue-walled street inside Santa Catalina, the walled convent-town of white volcanic sillar stone in Arequipa. At 2,335 m it is a gentle first day in the Andes before the high passes.

commonsFile: File:Islas flotantes de los Uros, Lago Titicaca, Perú, 2015-08-01, DD 44-48 PAN.jpg
alt: Panorama of the reed islands of the Uros community on Lake Titicaca
caption: The Uros reed islands near Puno, rebuilt continually from totora reeds. The visit is best done with a community-run boat, spending money directly with the families who live there.

alt: Terraced hillside and shoreline of Amantaní island on Lake Titicaca
caption: Amantaní, a farming island with no cars where the group sleeps in a family homestay at about 3,800 m. Evening meals and the climb to the summit ruins at sunset are part of the stay.

commonsFile: File:Plaza de Armas, Cusco, Perú, 2015-07-31, DD 53-56 PAN.jpg
alt: Panorama of the Plaza de Armas in Cusco with the cathedral and surrounding arcades
caption: The Plaza de Armas of Cusco, the Inca capital, ringed by Spanish colonial arcades built over Inca foundations. After the lake, the group spends a rest day here at 3,400 m.

commonsFile: File:View of Inca terraces of Moray, 2018.jpg
alt: Concentric circular Inca terraces at Moray
caption: The circular terraces at Moray, sunken bowls that agronomists have measured with temperature differences between levels. The site sits on the Maras plateau and is combined with the salt pans on a driven day through the Sacred Valley.

commonsFile: File:Salineras de Maras, Maras, Perú, 2015-07-30, DD 03-07 PAN.JPG
alt: Panorama of the terraced salt pans of Maras on a mountainside
caption: The Maras salt pans, thousands of small terraced pools fed by a salty spring and worked by local families. The pans are in use year-round, though wet-season rain can interrupt harvesting.

alt: Stone terraces and ruins above the town of Ollantaytambo
caption: The terraces and fortress above Ollantaytambo, a living Inca town whose street grid is still inhabited. The group sleeps here before the morning train to Machu Picchu.

alt: Panorama of Machu Picchu with Huayna Picchu behind the Inca citadel
caption: Machu Picchu seen from the classic viewpoint with Huayna Picchu behind. Entry is by timed ticket for one of the circuits; in the rainy season mist is common, and the cap is lower than in the June to November high season.

commonsFile: File:Machu Picchu - train runs right through the center of Aguas Calientes - IMG 7789.jpg
alt: A train running along the track through the centre of Aguas Calientes below Machu Picchu
caption: The railway running through the middle of Aguas Calientes, the town below Machu Picchu that can only be reached by train or on foot. Landslides and strikes occasionally close the line in the rainy season, so the last days of the trip keep a spare day.
